title: A kit track's step pattern exports as MIDI on the rack's pad notes
description:
As a beatmaker, I want my kit track's step pattern as MIDI on the rack's pad notes, so that it plays the exported rack the way Apricity plays the kit.

```gherkin
Feature: A kit track's notes exported as MIDI
  Background:
    Given a sample "brk.wav" of 2 bars in 4/4 at 120 BPM, analyzed
    And the score "flip.apr":
      """
      tempo 120
      time 4/4
      key C
      bars 2
      clip brk = brk.wav
      kit b = slice brk by beats 1
      track b steps "1 . 2 . 3 _ 4 ." grid 8
      """

  Scenario: Each step becomes a note on its pad's note
    When I export kit "b" from "flip.apr" with "--steps b"
    Then the export writes "b.adg" and "b.mid"
    And "b.mid" has 8 notes
    And the first note is C1 at beat 0 lasting 0.5 beats
    And the third note is D1 at beat 2 lasting 1 beat

  Scenario: The file carries the score's tempo and time signature
    When I export kit "b" from "flip.apr" with "--steps b"
    Then "b.mid" has tempo 120 BPM and time signature 4/4

  Scenario: Velocities are the notes' velocities
    Given the track line says steps "1@40 . 2! . 3 _ 4 ."
    When I export kit "b" from "flip.apr" with "--steps b"
    Then the first note has velocity 40
    And the second note has velocity 127
    And the third note has velocity 100

  Scenario: Swing and humanize move the notes as the compiler moved them
    Given the track line adds "swing 60 humanize 10ms 10%"
    When I export kit "b" from "flip.apr" with "--steps b"
    Then every note starts where the compiled timeline starts it, within one MIDI tick

  Scenario: A track that plays one pad plays that pad's note
    Given the score also has "track one = b.3 at 1 2"
    When I export kit "b" from "flip.apr" with "--steps one"
    Then "one.mid" has 2 notes, both on D1

  Scenario: A track limited to some bars keeps its place in the score (bar 1 is beat 0)
    Given the track line adds "bars 2"
    When I export kit "b" from "flip.apr" with "--steps b"
    Then the first note is at beat 4
```
